text.p: Building products company Hepworth Plc said in a statement on Monday that its chief executive John Carter has resigned, with effect from today, "for personal reasons."
A spokesman for the building materials group said Carter's departure was "amicable" and based on "mutual agreement" and that the former chief executive was leaving to pursue other interests.

Carter who is 51 years old has been chief executive at Hepworth for five years and joined the company in 1987. Hepworth was informed of the sudden resignation earlier on Monday but the company spokesman denied there was any rupture over strategy or disagreement behind the news.
The group has started its search for a replacement and an announcement will be made in due course.
Carter's resignation comes just ahead of a changeover of the chairmanship, with Jeremy Lancaster due to takeover as chairman from Sir Roland Smith.
In recent weeks, Hepworth reported year pretax profits of 67.6 million pounds, a fall of 9.3 percent on the previous year due to redundancy and pension costs.
The group had warned that the strong pound and rising pension costs would continue to eat into profits in the current financial year.
Hepworth also announced the sale of its refractories business to Alpine Group Inc of the U.S. for 62.5 million stg last week. It said the proceeds would be used to cut debt.
